  k_folds: 5              # number of contiguous water-year blocks
  n_evals: 1000           # DDS model runs per calibration (per fold)

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, dpi = 120)
source(here::here("scripts/00_setup.R"))
```

# Purpose

Baseline process model for the shared test gauges, and the template for
how every later model (distributed, other routing, LSTM) gets evaluated.

1. GridMET basin-mean forcing → `wbm_run()` → daily runoff (mm)
2. Runoff → `route_ihacres()` → streamflow (mm/day)
3. WBM and routing parameters calibrated **jointly** on KGE with
   Dynamically Dimensioned Search (DDS; Tolson & Shoemaker 2007), a
   derivative-free optimizer built for small run budgets
4. 5-fold **blocked** cross-validation on contiguous water-year blocks
   (WY1981 is warm-up and never scored)
5. Test-fold skill compared with a day-of-year climatology benchmark fit on
   the same training years

What changed from the MORA workflow: the WBM and routing parameters are
fit together (MORA fit runoff first, then routing). Every metric is
reported on held-out water years. The fold design is shared with every
other model in this repo.

To run with different settings, knit with parameters, e.g.
`rmarkdown::render("scripts/03_wbm_ihacres_cv.Rmd", params = list(pet_method = "gridmet"))`.
Results are cached per gauge, so re-knitting only recalibrates gauges that
have no cached result, or whose cached result was made with different
bounds or calibration settings (or all of them with `rerun = TRUE`).

```{r paths}
pet_method <- params$pet_method
out_dir <- params$out_dir %||%
  here::here("data", "processed", "results", paste0("wbm_ihacres_", pet_method))
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Gauges are identified by site number + official USGS station name only, so
# swapping a gauge in config/test_gauges.csv needs no changes here.
gauges <- get_test_gauges()

# A gauge is usable once scripts/02_get_data.R has written its inputs
gauges$has_data <- file.exists(here::here("data", "processed", gauges$site_no, "daily.parquet"))
gauge_levels <- gauges$gauge_label   # fixed facet/legend order
knitr::kable(dplyr::select(gauges, gauge_label, state, ecoregion, drain_sqkm, has_data),
             digits = 0, col.names = c("Gauge", "State", "GAGES-II ecoregion", "Area (km²)", "Data ready"))
```

```{r load-data}
# Read each gauge's model-ready daily table and static WBM parameters
inputs <- gauges %>%
  dplyr::filter(has_data) %>%
  dplyr::pull(site_no) %>%
  rlang::set_names() %>%
  purrr::map(function(site) list(
    daily = arrow::read_parquet(here::here("data", "processed", site, "daily.parquet")),
    static = readr::read_csv(here::here("data", "processed", site, "static.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  ))

label_of <- function(site) factor(gauges$gauge_label[match(site, gauges$site_no)], levels = gauge_levels)
```

# Inputs at a glance

Look at the climate and flow regimes before calibrating anything. The water
balance model can only work if the climate inputs and the observed flow are
roughly consistent: runoff ratios above ~1, or a big mismatch in the
timing of the seasonal cycle, point to forcing or area problems rather
than model problems.

```{r static-table}
purrr::imap_dfr(inputs, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$static, site_no = .y)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::select(gauge, elev_m, slope_deg, aspect_deg, swc_max_mm, jtemp_c, kc_dormant, kc_growing, lat) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Basin-mean static WBM parameters")
```

```{r annual-balance, fig.height = 4}
# Water-year totals: precipitation vs. observed runoff. The runoff ratio Q/P
# is the first sanity check on forcing and drainage area.
annual <- purrr::imap_dfr(inputs, function(x, site) {
  x$daily %>%
    dplyr::filter(wy > min(wy)) %>%                          # drop the warm-up year
    dplyr::group_by(wy) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(P = sum(prcp_mm), Q = sum(q_mm), PET_ref = sum(pet_ref_mm),
                     frac_obs = mean(!is.na(q_mm)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(site_no = site)
}) %>%
  dplyr::filter(frac_obs > 0.95) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no))

annual %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(P = mean(P), Q = mean(Q), runoff_ratio = mean(Q / P),
                   aridity = mean(PET_ref / P), n_wy = dplyr::n()) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mean annual totals (mm) for complete water years; aridity = GridMET reference ET / P")

ggplot(annual, aes(P, Q, color = gauge)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Water-year precipitation (mm)", y = "Water-year runoff (mm)", color = NULL,
       subtitle = "Points above the dashed line have more runoff than precipitation") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

```{r monthly-regime, fig.height = 7}
# Mean monthly cycle of precipitation, temperature, and observed flow: shows
# snow-dominated (Q lags P) vs. rain-dominated (Q tracks P) regimes.
monthly <- purrr::imap_dfr(inputs, function(x, site) {
  x$daily %>%
    dplyr::mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(month) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(`P (mm/day)` = mean(prcp_mm), `Q obs (mm/day)` = mean(q_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
                     `T mean (°C)` = mean(tmean_c), .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(site_no = site)
}) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(month, site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no))

ggplot(monthly, aes(month, value, color = name)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Model and parameters

The model is a chain of two pieces:

- **Water balance (`wbm_run`)**: rain and snow split on the Jennings rain–snow
  threshold temperature, degree-day snowmelt, PET, and a soil bucket that
  dries exponentially. Any water the soil can't hold is that day's runoff.
- **PET**: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith grass reference ET (ETo) from GridMET
  temperature, shortwave radiation, humidity, and 10 m wind (converted to
  2 m), times a crop coefficient. Kc is **not calibrated**: each basin's
  dormant- and growing-season Kc are area-weighted from NLCD 2019 upstream
  land cover (`inst/extdata/kc_nlcd.csv`), and daily Kc ramps between them on a
  15-day trailing mean temperature (fully dormant ≤ 2 °C, fully growing
  ≥ 10 °C). PET is 0 when snowpack exceeds 2 mm SWE. This replaces the
  calibrated `pet_mult`, so PET error can no longer be absorbed by a free
  multiplier.
- **Routing (`route_ihacres`)**: runoff is split between a quick and a slow
  linear reservoir; an optional fraction is lost to deep groundwater.

The WBM's own excess-water store (`return_rate`) does the same job as the
routing stores, so it's fixed at 1 to avoid two parameters trading off.
The routing `delay` is a whole number of days (0–2). DDS searches it
directly. Basins under ~600 km² should mostly need a 0–1 day lag, plus any
offset between the GridMET day (ending ~12 UTC) and the USGS calendar day.

```{r bounds}
# Calibration ranges. Equal lower/upper bounds fix a parameter.
# Widened after the first PM x Kc run, where fits sat on these bounds:
# hock = 1 (Duckabush, Sycamore), soil_mult = 0.3 (Chattooga) and ~3
# (Duckabush), tau_q = 15 (Crystal), jtemp_offset ~2 (Crystal).
# Previous results: data/processed/results/wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith_bounds_v1/
bounds <- param_bounds(
  hock         = c(0.5, 8),     # degree-day melt factor (mm °C⁻¹ day⁻¹)
  jtemp_offset = c(-3, 3),      # shift on the rain/snow threshold (°C)
  soil_mult    = c(0.1, 5),     # multiplier on soil water capacity
  tau_q        = c(0.5, 30),    # quickflow recession (days)
  tau_s        = c(10, 400),    # slowflow recession (days)
  vs           = c(0.05, 0.95), # fraction of runoff routed through the slow store
  loss         = c(0, 0.5),     # fraction lost to deep groundwater
  delay        = c(0, 2),       # routing lag (whole days)
  .integer = "delay"
)
wbm_pars <- c("hock", "jtemp_offset", "soil_mult")
knitr::kable(bounds, caption = "Calibration bounds")

# Build the closure the calibrator calls: parameters in, simulated
# streamflow (mm/day) out, aligned day-for-day with the observations.
make_model_fn <- function(daily, static, return_wbm = FALSE) {
  function(p) {
    wb <- wbm_run(daily, c(as.list(static), p[wbm_pars]), pet_method = pet_method)
    q <- route_ihacres(wb$runoff, tau_q = p$tau_q, tau_s = p$tau_s, vs = p$vs,
                       loss = p$loss, delay = p$delay)
    if (return_wbm) dplyr::mutate(wb, q_sim = q) else q
  }
}
```

# Cross-validation design

The water years after the warm-up are cut into `r params$k_folds`
contiguous blocks. In fold *i*, block *i* is the test set and all other
blocks are training. The model always runs the **whole** record (it needs
continuous snow and soil states); the fold only decides which days count
toward the objective. Because nothing about the test years enters
calibration except through the model state, no buffer is needed here.
LSTMs will need a buffer at least as long as their input sequence.

```{r fold-layout, fig.height = 2.5}
example_dates <- inputs[[1]]$daily$date
folds_example <- make_blocked_folds(example_dates, k = params$k_folds, warmup_years = 1)
folds_example %>%
  dplyr::distinct(fold, wy, role) %>%
  ggplot(aes(wy, factor(fold), fill = role)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(train = "#9ecae1", test = "#b02a24", warmup = "grey70")) +
  labs(x = "Water year", y = "Fold", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Calibrate and cross-validate

Each gauge's results are saved to `r out_dir` as soon as that gauge
finishes, so an interrupted run keeps the gauges it completed. Within a
gauge the `r params$k_folds` folds are calibrated in parallel on
`r params$n_cores` cores; each fold uses its own fixed seed, so results are
identical whatever `n_cores` is.

```{r run-cv}
# Settings that change the calibration result. A cached result is reused
# only if it was made with exactly these, including the gauge's static
# inputs (so editing inst/extdata/kc_nlcd.csv and re-running 02_get_data.R
# triggers recalibration).
cv_settings <- list(pet_method = pet_method, k_folds = params$k_folds,
                    n_evals = params$n_evals, bounds = bounds)

run_gauge_cv <- function(site) {
  cache <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(site, "_cv.rds"))
  site_settings <- c(cv_settings, list(static = as.list(inputs[[site]]$static)))
  if (file.exists(cache) && !isTRUE(params$rerun)) {
    cached <- readRDS(cache)
    if (isTRUE(all.equal(cached$settings, site_settings))) return(cached)
    message(site, ": cached result used different settings; recalibrating")
  }

  x <- inputs[[site]]
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x$daily$prcp_mm), !anyNA(x$daily$tmean_c))
  obs <- x$daily$q_mm
  model_fn <- make_model_fn(x$daily, x$static)
  folds <- make_blocked_folds(x$daily$date, k = params$k_folds, warmup_years = 1)

  t0 <- Sys.time()
  cv <- cross_validate_model(model_fn, bounds, obs, folds, objective = kge,
                             n_evals = params$n_evals, n_cores = params$n_cores, seed = 1)

  # Lower benchmark on the identical folds: mean flow for each day of year,
  # estimated from the training years only
  bench <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(params$k_folds), function(f) {
    fd <- folds[folds$fold == f, ]
    b <- benchmark_doy_climatology(obs, fd$date, fd$role == "train")
    te <- fd$role == "test"
    dplyr::mutate(eval_metrics(obs[te], b[te]), fold = f, set = "test", .before = 1)
  })

  res <- list(
    metrics = dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::mutate(cv$metrics, model = "WBM + IHACRES"),
                               dplyr::mutate(bench, model = "DOY climatology")),
    params = cv$params,
    sims = cv$sims,
    traces = cv$traces,
    settings = site_settings,
    minutes = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))
  )
  saveRDS(res, cache)
  res
}

cv_results <- purrr::map(rlang::set_names(names(inputs)), run_gauge_cv)

# Stack per-gauge results into tidy tables
metrics <- purrr::imap_dfr(cv_results, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$metrics, site_no = .y))
cv_params <- purrr::imap_dfr(cv_results, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$params, site_no = .y))
sims <- purrr::imap_dfr(cv_results, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$sims, site_no = .y))
traces <- purrr::imap_dfr(cv_results, ~ dplyr::mutate(.x$traces, site_no = .y))

readr::write_csv(metrics, file.path(out_dir, "cv_metrics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(cv_params, file.path(out_dir, "cv_params.csv"))
arrow::write_parquet(sims, file.path(out_dir, "cv_test_sims.parquet"))

tibble::tibble(gauge = label_of(names(cv_results)),
               minutes = purrr::map_dbl(cv_results, "minutes")) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Calibration time per gauge (cached gauges show their original run time)")
```

# Results

## Calibration convergence

Best training KGE found so far vs. number of model runs, one line per fold.
Curves that are still climbing at the end mean `n_evals` is too small for
that gauge; flat tails mean runs are being wasted and `n_evals` can drop.

```{r convergence, fig.height = 4}
traces %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(objective > -1) %>%                 # hide the penalty floor from failed early runs
  ggplot(aes(eval, objective, group = fold)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1b6ca8", alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  labs(x = "Model runs", y = "Best training KGE so far") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```

## Skill on held-out water years

Each point is one test fold. The model is only useful where it clearly beats
the day-of-year climatology. KGE > −0.41 already beats the *mean-flow*
benchmark (Knoben et al. 2019), so compare against the climatology points,
not against zero.

```{r skill-plot, fig.height = 5}
test_metrics <- metrics %>%
  dplyr::filter(set == "test") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no))

test_metrics %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(kge, nse, log_nse), names_to = "metric") %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, gauge, color = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("WBM + IHACRES" = "#1b6ca8", "DOY climatology" = "grey40")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

test_metrics %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, model) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(c(kge, nse, log_nse, pbias), median), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median across test folds")
```

## Overfitting check: train vs. test

A large drop from train to test means the parameters are fitting
noise in the calibration years rather than the basin's behavior.

```{r train-test, fig.height = 4}
metrics %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == "WBM + IHACRES") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no)) %>%
  dplyr::select(gauge, fold, set, kge) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = kge) %>%
  ggplot(aes(train, test, color = gauge)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "KGE (train)", y = "KGE (test)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "right")
```

## Why the fit is good or bad: KGE components

KGE combines correlation (*r*, timing), variability ratio (*α*, flashiness),
and bias ratio (*β*, volume); ideal is 1 for each. Pulling the components
apart shows which part of the hydrograph the model gets wrong.

```{r kge-components, fig.height = 4}
test_metrics %>%
  dplyr::filter(model == "WBM + IHACRES") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(kge_r, kge_alpha, kge_beta), names_to = "component") %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, gauge)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = 2, color = "grey50") +
  geom_point(color = "#1b6ca8", alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ component, scales = "free_x",
             labeller = as_labeller(c(kge_r = "r (timing)", kge_alpha = "α (variability)", kge_beta = "β (bias)"))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Parameter stability across folds

If a parameter swings across its whole range from fold to fold while
skill stays similar, it is poorly identified (equifinality). Those
parameters are candidates to fix or to tie to basin attributes.

```{r param-stability, fig.height = 6}
cv_params %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no)) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(bounds$param[bounds$lower < bounds$upper]), names_to = "param") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(bounds, by = "param") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(scaled = (value - lower) / (upper - lower)) %>%   # 0 = lower bound, 1 = upper
  ggplot(aes(scaled, gauge)) +
  geom_point(color = "#1b6ca8", alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ param, ncol = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Position within calibration bounds (0 = lower, 1 = upper)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Points piled on 0 or 1 mean the bound is limiting the fit") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Hydrographs (out-of-fold predictions)

Every day shown was predicted by parameters that never saw that water year.

```{r hydrographs, fig.height = 10}
sims_l <- sims %>% dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no))

sims_l %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no) %>%
  dplyr::filter(date >= max(date) - 3 * 365) %>%             # last 3 water years
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(obs, sim), names_to = "series", values_to = "q_mm") %>%
  ggplot(aes(date, q_mm, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(obs = "black", sim = "#1b6ca8")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Streamflow (mm/day)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Flow duration curves

Highlights high- and low-flow errors that daily efficiency scores average
over. The log scale makes low-flow behavior visible.

```{r fdc, fig.height = 6}
sims_l %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(obs, sim), names_to = "series", values_to = "q_mm") %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(q_mm)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, series) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(exceedance = 1 - (rank(q_mm, ties.method = "first") - 0.5) / dplyr::n()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(exceedance, pmax(q_mm, 1e-3), color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(obs = "black", sim = "#1b6ca8")) +
  labs(x = "Exceedance probability", y = "Streamflow (mm/day, log)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Seasonal cycle

Errors in the mean monthly hydrograph usually come from snow (timing of
melt) or PET (summer recession).

```{r seasonal, fig.height = 6}
sims_l %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(gauge, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(obs = mean(obs, na.rm = TRUE), sim = mean(sim), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(obs, sim), names_to = "series", values_to = "q_mm") %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, q_mm, color = series)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ gauge, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(obs = "black", sim = "#1b6ca8")) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = "Mean streamflow (mm/day)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Internal water balance

Re-run each gauge with its median cross-validated parameters to look at
the internal fluxes. Implausible snowpack or AET here can explain a
good-looking hydrograph that is right for the wrong reasons.

```{r internal-fluxes, fig.height = 7}
median_params <- cv_params %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(bounds$param), median), .groups = "drop")

internal <- purrr::map_dfr(names(inputs), function(site) {
  p <- as.list(dplyr::filter(median_params, site_no == site)[bounds$param])
  make_model_fn(inputs[[site]]$daily, inputs[[site]]$static, return_wbm = TRUE)(p) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(site_no = site)
})

internal %>%
  dplyr::filter(calc_water_year(date) > min(calc_water_year(date))) %>%   # drop warm-up
  dplyr::mutate(month = as.integer(format(date, "%m"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no, month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(Snowpack = mean(snowpack), `Soil water` = mean(soil),
                   ETo = mean(pet_ref) * 30, PET = mean(pet) * 30, AET = mean(aet) * 30,
                   Runoff = mean(runoff) * 30,
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(site_no, month)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no),
                type = ifelse(name %in% c("Snowpack", "Soil water"), "Storage (mm)", "Flux (mm/month)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, value, color = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(type ~ gauge, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(gauge = label_wrap_gen(18))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 4, 7, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Month", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Long-term water budget check

Over many years, storage change is negligible in these reference basins,
so mean observed P − Q approximates mean actual ET. It's an independent
check on PET and Kc that doesn't depend on calibration: modeled AET far
below P − Q means PET is too low, and the calibration will then use other
parameters (bigger soil bucket, groundwater `loss`) to get rid of the
extra water.

```{r water-budget}
internal %>%
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::bind_rows(purrr::imap(inputs, ~ dplyr::select(.x$daily, date, q_mm) %>%
                                                  dplyr::mutate(site_no = .y))),
                   by = c("site_no", "date")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(calc_water_year(date) > min(calc_water_year(date))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(site_no) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(yrs = dplyr::n() / 365.25,
                   P = sum(prcp) / yrs, ETo = sum(pet_ref) / yrs, PET = sum(pet) / yrs,
                   AET_model = sum(aet) / yrs,
                   `P - Q obs` = (sum(prcp[!is.na(q_mm)]) - sum(q_mm, na.rm = TRUE)) / (sum(!is.na(q_mm)) / 365.25)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gauge = label_of(site_no), `AET / (P - Q)` = AET_model / `P - Q obs`) %>%
  dplyr::select(gauge, P, ETo, PET, AET_model, `P - Q obs`, `AET / (P - Q)`) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2), caption = "Mean annual water budget (mm/yr), median CV parameters, WY1982-2024")
```

# Experiment log

What has been tried in this notebook, in order, and what was learned.
Each run's outputs are kept in its own folder under
`data/processed/results/`; the table below is rebuilt from those folders
when they exist.

| Run | Folder | PET | Kc | Calibrated params | Bounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `wbm_ihacres_oudin` | Oudin (heat-load adjusted) | none | + `pet_mult` (0.6–1.6) | original |
| 2 | `wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith_bounds_v1` | FAO-56 PM ETo | placeholder table | `pet_mult` removed | original |
| 3 | `wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith` (**current**) | FAO-56 PM ETo | placeholder table | `pet_mult` removed | widened |
| 4 | `wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith_kc_liu2017` | FAO-56 PM ETo | Liu et al. (2017) FLUXNET | `pet_mult` removed | widened |
| 5a | `lstm_single_basin_val_last` (notebook 04) | none (ETo is an input) | none | LSTM weights; 3-seed ensemble; validation = last 5 training WY | n/a |
| 5b | `lstm_single_basin` (notebook 04) | none (ETo is an input) | none | as 5a; validation = 5 WY spread across training | n/a |
| 6 | `gr4j_cemaneige` (notebook 05) | FAO-56 PM ETo | placeholder table | X1-X4, C1, C2 (6 params) | airGR defaults |

Original bounds: `hock` 1–8, `jtemp_offset` ±2, `soil_mult` 0.3–3,
`tau_q` 0.5–15. Widened: `hock` 0.5–8, `jtemp_offset` ±3, `soil_mult`
0.1–5, `tau_q` 0.5–30. All runs: DDS with 1,000 runs per fold, 5 blocked
folds, KGE objective.

```{r experiment-log}
runs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~run, ~folder,
  "1 Oudin + pet_mult",          "wbm_ihacres_oudin",
  "2 PM x Kc (placeholder)",     "wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith_bounds_v1",
  "3 PM x Kc, wide bounds",      "wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith",
  "4 PM x Kc (Liu 2017)",        "wbm_ihacres_penman_monteith_kc_liu2017",
  "5a LSTM (val = last 5 WY)",   "lstm_single_basin_val_last",
  "5b LSTM (val spread)",        "lstm_single_basin",
  "6 CemaNeige-GR4J",            "gr4j_cemaneige"
)
log_metrics <- purrr::pmap_dfr(runs, function(run, folder) {
  f <- here::here("data", "processed", "results", folder, "cv_metrics.csv")
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(NULL)
  readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::filter(set == "test", model %in% c("WBM + IHACRES", "LSTM (single basin)", "CemaNeige-GR4J")) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(run = run)
})
if (nrow(log_metrics) > 0) {
  log_metrics %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gauge = label_of(site_no), run) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(KGE = median(kge), `log-NSE` = median(log_nse), .groups = "drop") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = c(KGE, `log-NSE`), names_glue = "{.value} | {run}") %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median test-fold skill by run")
}
```

**Run 1 → 2 (Oudin to Penman-Monteith × Kc).** Oudin PET was only 40–65%
of FAO-56 ETo at every basin, and the calibration made up for it with
`pet_mult` > 1 and a soil multiplier pinned at its upper bound (3) at
Swift, Chattooga, and Duckabush. Switching to PM × land-cover Kc and
removing `pet_mult` kept KGE about the same with one fewer free
parameter, and Swift's soil multiplier dropped to 0.5–1.1 with much
better low flows (log-NSE −0.05 → 0.30).

**Run 2 → 3 (widened bounds).** Parameters sitting on bounds were given
room. Test KGE moved by only ±0.02, so the bounds were not the main limit.
Low flows improved at Chattooga and Sycamore but got much worse at
Duckabush (a larger bucket traded low-flow fit for KGE). Remaining signs
of structural or forcing problems: Duckabush still wants a very large
bucket (likely GridMET precipitation undercatch: observed runoff is 86%
of P), Chattooga wants a very small one (Kc probably too high for mixed
forest), and `hock` is unidentifiable at rain-dominated Chattooga.

**Run 3 → 4 (Liu et al. 2017 Kc), rejected.** The forest, shrub,
grassland, and crop rows were replaced with FLUXNET seasonal Kc from Liu
et al. (2017, Table 1; FAO-56 grass ETo basis; dormant = Nov–Jan mean,
growing = largest seasonal mean). Basin Kc fell by roughly 40%
(e.g. Chattooga 0.59/0.98 → 0.36/0.62). Modeled AET then fell well below
the long-term water budget (Duckabush 193 vs. 358 mm/yr P − Q; Crystal
219 vs. 387; Swift 384 vs. 568; Chattooga 706 vs. 844; Sycamore 448
vs. 494). The calibration compensated by pushing `soil_mult` to its new
upper bound (5) and raising groundwater `loss` at every basin, and test
skill dropped (Sycamore KGE 0.58 → 0.35; log-NSE fell at Swift,
Chattooga, and Crystal). **Cause:** Liu et al. report *actual* Kc
(AET/ETo), which already includes water stress and snow-covered winters.
This model applies both limits again (soil bucket, zero ET under snow),
so actual Kc double counts them. They are a lower bound on the
*potential* Kc this model needs. The table was reverted to the
placeholder potential Kc; the Liu table is archived in
`inst/extdata/kc_nlcd_liu2017.csv`.

**Runs 5-6 (LSTM and GR4J comparisons; see notebooks 04 and 05).** On
the same test days, the single-basin LSTM beat WBM + IHACRES on low flows
at four basins (log-NSE 0.69-0.86) but failed at intermittent Sycamore
Creek (KGE 0.08), where the last-5-years validation block was too dry for
early stopping to work (run 5a). Run 5b spreads the 5 validation water
years across the training period instead: Sycamore's models now train a
median of 36 epochs (vs. 2), and its test KGE rose from 0.08 to 0.38,
still well short of GR4J (0.76) and the WBM (0.58). The other basins
changed by -0.03 to +0.02 KGE. A single-basin LSTM remains data-limited
for intermittent flow, where a few events carry most of the volume (the
top 1% of days hold 48% of Sycamore's flow). CemaNeige-GR4J, with the same forcing, PET, folds,
and calibration but 6 parameters instead of 8, matched or beat the WBM
everywhere (median test KGE 0.76-0.86), most clearly at Sycamore (0.76
vs. 0.58) and on Duckabush low flows (log-NSE 0.76 vs. -0.48). So the
WBM's weaknesses are largely structural (single-elevation snow, soil
bucket, routing), not inherent to the forcing.

**Current configuration:** run 3. The vegetated Kc values are still
placeholders (informed judgment, not literature values). Candidates for a
principled replacement: FAO-56 / Allen & Pereira (2009) potential Kc from
canopy cover and height, or MODIS vegetation-index Kc. Either can be
tested with the water budget check above plus this CV.

# Notes and next steps

- Compare PET methods by re-knitting with `params = list(pet_method = "gridmet")`
  (GridMET's own ETo x the same Kc) or `"oudin"`; each writes to its own
  results folder. The Oudin run in `wbm_ihacres_oudin/` used a calibrated
  `pet_mult`, so compare it knowing that.
- Kc values in `inst/extdata/kc_nlcd.csv` are placeholders; after editing, re-run
  `scripts/02_get_data.R` (fast, everything else is cached) and re-knit.
- Parameters that hit their bounds or swing between folds are the first
  candidates to fix or constrain.
- The fold tables and `eval_metrics()` outputs here are the comparison
  format for the distributed, routing, and LSTM experiments.
